sage-console.alt: A SAGE air-defense operator console: a large round display screen set in a gray panel of switches, with a pistol-shaped light gun resting on the desk
sage-console.caption: An operator’s console from the SAGE air-defense system, with its light gun, at the Computer History Museum. SAGE’s radar sites and computers were linked by modems over telephone lines.

teletype-33.alt: A Teletype Model 33: a beige electromechanical terminal with a typewriter-style keyboard, a roll of printed paper, and a paper-tape punch and reader on its left side
teletype-33.caption: A Teletype Model 33, photographed in 2025. Electromechanical terminals like this are what low-speed modems were first built to connect.

novation-cat.alt: A flat black acoustic-coupler modem with two round rubber cups on top, and a cream-colored telephone handset lying beside it
novation-cat.caption: An acoustic coupler: a Novation CAT, sold from 1979. The telephone handset is pressed into the two rubber cups, mouthpiece over the modem’s loudspeaker and earpiece over its microphone. No wire connects the modem to the telephone network.
novation-cat.credit: Photo: G. Edward Johnson, via Wikimedia Commons

pennywhistle.alt: Black-and-white product illustration of the Pennywhistle 103: a low rectangular box with two round wells on top for a telephone handset and a row of small switches on the front
pennywhistle.caption: The Pennywhistle 103, from the kit’s 1976 documentation. The two wells hold a telephone handset.
pennywhistle.credit: M&R Electronics, Inc., via Wikimedia Commons
pennywhistle.license: public domain in the United States (published 1976 without a copyright notice, according to its Commons page)

felsenstein.alt: Lee Felsenstein, a man with gray hair and glasses in a blue shirt, smiling beside a microphone
felsenstein.caption: Lee Felsenstein in 2007.
felsenstein.credit: Photo: Marcin Wichary, cropped by Gorinin, via Wikimedia Commons

atari-coupler.alt: A home computer keyboard on a desk beside an acoustic modem with an orange telephone handset seated in its cups, a rotary telephone, and a cassette recorder
atari-coupler.caption: Going online at home, early 1980s style: an Atari 800XL, a Radio Shack acoustic modem with the handset in place, the telephone it belongs to, and a cassette recorder for storage. A 2019 exhibition setup.
atari-coupler.credit: Photo: Wolfgang Stief, via Wikimedia Commons
atari-coupler.changes: Cropped at the top and resized

bbs-login.alt: A text-only screen: a login prompt asking for a user name and password, a message of the day, and a main menu of lettered choices such as Msgs Areas, File Areas and Chat Rooms
bbs-login.caption: What a caller saw: log in, read the message of the day, pick a letter. This is a 2010 screenshot of a modern revival of the Telegard BBS software, not a period capture.
bbs-login.credit: Screenshot: Chris Tusa, via Wikimedia Commons

baudot.alt: Engraved portrait of Émile Baudot, a bearded man in a dark coat
baudot.caption: Émile Baudot, in an engraving made before 1903.
baudot.credit: Engraving: A. Delzers, via Wikimedia Commons

modem-stack.alt: Six external modems of the early 1990s stacked on top of one another, their front panels showing rows of indicator lights
modem-stack.caption: A stack of early-1990s external modems, among them a USRobotics Courier V.32 bis and a Hayes Optima.
modem-stack.credit: Photo: Szumyk (as attributed by Wikimedia Commons)

sportster-336.alt: A dark gray external modem with a curved top and the words Sportster Voice 33.6 Faxmodem on its front edge
sportster-336.caption: A USRobotics Sportster Voice 33.6 external modem.

shannon.alt: Claude Shannon, a slender man in a tweed jacket and tie, in a studio portrait
shannon.caption: Claude Shannon, about 1956.
shannon.credit: Bell Telephone Laboratories; scan by Tekniska museet (CC BY 2.0), via Wikimedia Commons
shannon.license: public domain in the United States (published 1956 without a copyright notice, according to its Commons page)

sportster-56k.alt: A dark gray external modem with the words Sportster Voice 56K Faxmodem on its front edge
sportster-56k.caption: The same box, one generation on: a USRobotics Sportster 56K.

adsl-modem.alt: A small white DSL modem with a row of indicator lights on its front
adsl-modem.caption: A DSL modem (a Deutsche Telekom Teledat 431).

cable-modem.alt: A black upright cable modem with a column of indicator lights
cable-modem.caption: A cable modem (a Motorola SurfBoard for the European version of DOCSIS 3.0). Neither box makes a sound.
